summary: Reviewed MovieEditorView.axaml and api-surface.md. All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed. Implementation follows established project patterns correctly.

ListBox with ActorList/SelectedActorIndex TwoWay binding is idiomatic and correct. The [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor] decorators on _selectedActorIndex correctly drive MoveActorUpCommand/MoveActorDownCommand re-evaluation — no IsEnabled attribute needed.

TaggerView embedded with DataContext='{Binding TaggerVm}' compiles correctly against MovieEditorViewModel (which has TaggerViewModel? TaggerVm). TaggerView's own x:DataType='vm:TaggerViewModel' establishes its inner compiled binding scope independently — correct Avalonia pattern.
MoveActorUp/Down guard functions (CanMoveActorUp: index > 0; CanMoveActorDown: index >= 0 && index < Count-1) are correct and symmetric.
api-surface.md updated correctly: ActorList, SelectedActorIndex, TaggerVm, MoveActorUpCommand, MoveActorDownCommand all properly documented with accurate CanExecute descriptions.

TaggerViewModel lifecycle concern (ITagsManager.DataChanged subscription) is pre-existing technical debt documented in constraints.md (line 74-75) and deferred to a future IDisposable WP — out of scope for WP-022 whose scope is explicitly limited to MovieEditorView.axaml AXAML changes.

comments.note: No blocking issues found. The three changes (TaggerView wiring, ActorList ListBox, Cover Image label) are minimal, targeted, and architecturally consistent. No over-engineering observed.

[documentation-forward] constraints.md line 74 states 'Any host view that instantiates a TaggerViewModel must unsubscribe from ITagsManager.DataChanged in its Unloaded handler.' With WP-022's implementation, TaggerViewModel is instantiated by MovieEditorViewModel.LoadAsync (the ViewModel), not by MovieEditorView (the host view). Update the constraint language from 'host view' to 'Any component (view or ViewModel) that instantiates a TaggerViewModel...' to accurately reflect the ViewModel-owned pattern and prevent future confusion.

summary: WP-022 documentation pass: clarified TaggerViewModel lifecycle ownership contract in both api-surface.md and constraints.md to specify that the owning component (MovieEditorViewModel, not just 'the host view') bears responsibility for unsubscribing ITagsManager.DataChanged.
